name: OR-02
label: Likely R

key_factors: Incumbent Bentz has a large financial advantage ($1.4M vs $54K cash)
Prediction markets price Bentz at ~94% to win
No public polling or expert ratings to shift the picture
model.rationale: This eastern Oregon seat is firmly Republican, and incumbent Cliff Bentz holds an overwhelming fundraising edge over Democrat Chris Beck, who has raised under $100K. Markets price a Bentz win at about 94%, and no polls or ratings suggest the race is competitive.
model.watch: A surprise influx of outside spending for Beck or a major Bentz scandal could make this marginally closer, though the district's lean makes an upset very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Oregon's second district covers the state's rural east and south, and its R+14 partisan lean makes it the most Republican seat in Oregon. Cliff Bentz, the incumbent, is running for reelection after clearing his primary, while Democrat Chris Beck enters the general as a first-time challenger.

The financial picture is lopsided: Bentz has raised over $1 million and holds $1.4 million on hand, compared with Beck's $95,000 raised and $54,000 in the bank. No outside groups are active, no public polls exist, and prediction markets give Bentz roughly a 94% chance of winning. The race is rated Safe Republican.
